name: Arugula
label: arugula rows

planting.note: 4 rows full-length (8 ft each) on a 4x8 bed; cut-and-come-again

bed30.note: 4 rows ~7 in apart across a 30-in bed; sow thick and thin to 2-3 in for baby leaf, ~6 in for full rosettes (Cornell)

watch_for: Flea beetles (shot-hole damage; cover with floating row cover from the day of sowing); downy mildew in cool wet weather; bolting under heat/drought stress.
watering: Keep soil evenly moist for fast, tender growth; drought makes leaves hot and hastens bolting.
method_notes: Sow every 2 weeks from early spring until ~3-4 weeks before first frost (Johnny's/Cornell). Cut leaves ~1 in above the crown for 2-3 regrowth cuts (5-14 days apart); plants bolt in summer heat, so shade warm-season plantings. Self-seeds readily. Late-summer sowings are hardy in a hoophouse or under row cover — MOFGA lists arugula among greens harvestable through December in Maine.
source: Cornell Garden-Based Learning arugula guide (spacing, succession, flea beetles, downy mildew); Johnny's Selected Seeds arugula key growing info; MOFGA Winter Greens (Dec harvest); Oregon State extension (40-50 days full size)

name: Mustard Greens
label: mustard rows

planting.note: 3 rows full-length on a 4x8 bed; baby-leaf band or bunching rows

bed30.note: 3 rows ~10 in apart; thin bunching types to ~6 in (Seed Savers 6-18 in); baby leaf: sow a 4-row band and skip thinning (Johnny's)

watch_for: Flea beetles (row cover from sowing — Johnny's); cabbage worms and loopers in fall (Bt); bolting in hot weather — plant spring and late summer, not midsummer.
watering: Even moisture for rapid growth; heat or drought stress makes leaves hotter and more bolt-prone.
method_notes: Fastest brassica: baby leaf in ~3 weeks, full bunches 12-18 in in ~6 weeks (Johnny's). Succession-sow every ~2 weeks; in Maine grow early spring and again from late July for fall — MOFGA keeps mustards into December and lists them for overwintering under cover. Cut-and-come-again above the basal plate.
source: Johnny's Selected Seeds mustard greens + baby-leaf brassicas key growing info ('Red Giant' 21 baby/45 full); Seed Savers Exchange mustard guide (thinning); MOFGA Winter Greens

name: Collards
label: collard plants

planting.note: 2 rows x 6 plants along 8 ft; big plants — needs the room

bed30.note: 2 rows ~15 in apart; space plants 12-18 in — collards grow to 3 ft tall (UMaine #4311) and are transplanted at 12-18 in per Johnny's

watch_for: Flea beetles plus imported cabbageworm and cabbage looper (exclude with row covers; Bt for wormy leaves); clubroot in acid wet soil and black rot — rotate out of brassicas for 3+ years (Johnny's tests seed for black rot/black leg).
watering: Consistent moisture keeps leaves tender; drought toughens them.
method_notes: Not succession-sown — make one spring planting (transplants 4-6 weeks before last frost) and one fall planting (seedlings started May, set out June-July, per Johnny's). Harvest outer leaves from the bottom up; the plant keeps producing. Frost sweetens the leaves — UMaine #4311 harvests collards until temperatures hit the midteens and into early December in Maine. 'Flash' 55 days, 'Top Bunch 2.0' ~75 (Johnny's).
source: UMaine Bulletin #4311 'Giving Garden' (frost sweetening, mid-teens hardiness, Dec harvest); Johnny's Selected Seeds collards key growing info + 'Flash' variety page; Clemson HGIC collards (spacing corroboration); MOFGA Winter Greens

name: Bok Choy
label: bok choy heads

planting.note: 3 rows x 8 plants; cut baby heads at 4-6 in for a denser early crop

bed30.note: 3 rows ~10 in apart; thin full-size heads to 10-12 in ('Joi Choi' spacing, Johnny's)

watch_for: Flea beetles (floating row cover from day of sowing — Johnny's); premature bolting when seedlings get nights below 50 F or are rootbound/stressed before planting out; harvest before flowering; aphids in fall.
watering: Even moisture at all times — any drought or setback stress triggers bolting.
method_notes: Fast (~50 days) but strictly cool-season: grow as a spring crop and again from late July for fall — the fall crop is the better one in Maine, where MOFGA harvests bok choy through December. Do not succession-sow through hot midsummer (plants bolt); Johnny's advises sowing early spring through midsummer only in mild climates or with protection. 'Joi Choi' (50 days), 'Mei Qing Choi' are cold/heat-tolerant standouts (Johnny's).
source: Johnny's Selected Seeds pac choi key growing info + 'Joi Choi' variety page (50 days, 10-12 in spacing); MOFGA Winter Greens (Oct-Dec harvest)

name: Tatsoi
label: tatsoi rows

planting.note: 3 rows full-length on a 4x8 bed; baby-leaf band or full rosettes

bed30.note: 3 rows; baby leaf: sow in a 4-row band, no thinning; full rosettes thin to 8-10 in (Johnny's)

watch_for: Flea beetles (row cover from sowing); cabbage worms and loopers (Bt — Johnny's); downy mildew on dense late-summer sowings; slugs in wet fall weather.
watering: Even moisture keeps leaves mild and quick-growing.
method_notes: Hardiest of the Asian greens: MOFGA keeps tatsoi through December in Maine and overwinters it under row cover or in a tunnel; Johnny's can sow it into late fall for overwintering in protection. Succession-sow every ~2 weeks through late summer (25 days to baby rosettes, 45 to full heads — Johnny's). Cut-and-come-again above the basal plate.
source: Johnny's Selected Seeds tatsoi variety page (25 baby/45 full) + Asian greens and baby-leaf brassicas key growing info; MOFGA Winter Greens

name: Endive
label: endive hearts

planting.note: 2 rows x 10 plants at ~10 in spacing

bed30.note: 2 rows ~15 in apart; spacing 8-10 in encourages self-blanching hearts (Johnny's); direct-seeded rows thinned to 8 in

watch_for: Aphids on young plants; slugs in wet weather; bolting and tipburn under heat (choose tipburn-tolerant types like 'Benefine' — Johnny's); seed goes thermally dormant above 77 F, so germinate cool (60-68 F).
watering: Steady moisture — drought causes tipburn on the leaf edges and speeds bolting.
method_notes: Transplant for earliest heads (3-4 week-old seedlings); properly hardened transplants survive 20 F (Johnny's). Succession-sow every 3 weeks. Days-to-maturity listed are from transplant — add ~14-21 days when direct seeding; baby leaf is ready in 4-5 weeks (Johnny's). Fall is the prime crop in Maine: MOFGA harvests endive into December. Maine-recommended varieties: 'Salad King', 'Neos' (UMaine #2190). Self-blanches when tightly spaced; force a cream heart by covering the center 3 days before harvest (Johnny's French technique).
source: Johnny's Selected Seeds chicory endive/escarole key growing info + 'Benefine' variety page; UMaine Bulletin #2190 (Salad King, Neos varieties); MOFGA Winter Greens

name: Radicchio
label: radicchio heads

planting.note: 2 rows x 10 plants; succession-planting to find what heads in your site

bed30.note: 2 rows ~15 in apart; transplant 8-10 in apart, crown planted slightly above soil line to discourage bottom rot (Johnny's)

watch_for: Bolting, tipburn and bitterness under heat stress (UNH trials); bottom rot — transplant shallowly with the crown above soil (Johnny's); aphids. UNH found fewer than half of plants form marketable heads in a typical New England season — plant extra.
watering: Even moisture, especially as heads form; dry spells cause tipburn and bitter leaves.
method_notes: Treat as a fall crop in New England: Johnny's says radicchio grows best in cool weather (fall/winter/spring; summer only where nights stay below 60 F), and UNH variety trials (30+ cultivars) found chioggia types most reliably marketable with best disease resistance. ~80 days from transplant, add ~14 if direct seeded; succession-sow every 3 weeks (Johnny's). Seed germinates cool (60-68 F; thermally dormant above 77 F). 'Indigo' is Johnny's most sure-heading, tipburn-tolerant pick. Frost improves color and sweetness.
source: UNH radicchio variety trial (NHPR/UNH 2024, Sideman et al.); Johnny's Selected Seeds radicchio key growing info + 'Indigo' variety page; Oregon State extension (~80 days, 8-12 in spacing); MOFGA Winter Greens (overwintering greens list)

name: Sorrel
label: sorrel clumps

planting.note: 3 rows x ~10 plants, thinned to 8 in; clumps spread wide over the years

bed30.note: 3 rows ~10 in apart; thin to 8 in in-row (Johnny's bunching: 8 in apart, rows 12-18 in)

watch_for: Leaf miners tunnel in leaves (worst late spring through summer) — cut off and discard infested foliage and keep plants cut for regrowth; rust in humid weather; summer seed stalks lower leaf quality — keep them cut (Johnny's).
watering: Even moisture; light shade keeps summer leaves tender (Johnny's).
method_notes: Plant once — a hardy perennial (French type, zones 4-9 per Johnny's; MOFGA lists sorrel among overwintering Maine greens) giving some of the earliest spring and latest fall leaves. Days-to-maturity are for first harvest from seed (subtract ~14 if transplanting) — from year two it is simply there. Harvest outer leaves until established, then cut whole clumps above the crown; plants re-grow in fall even after bolting. Divide crowded clumps. Start indoors or direct-sow midspring through midsummer (Johnny's).
source: Johnny's Selected Seeds sorrel key growing info + 'Sorrel' (French type) variety page; MOFGA Winter Greens (overwintering greens list)
